newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- US T-bond vols build up ahead of payrolls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- US T-bond vols build up ahead of payrolls.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options inched up, despite dull range-trading in underlying instruments, as the market awaited Friday's October U.S. employment report, traders said.
Various technical indicators, including a triangle formation on the daily chart, seemed to point to a near-term breakout, increasing interest in options, they added.
"Vols have been firming up for a week," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. He said there were few sizeable deals today but added that volume should start picking up Tuesday.

Several other important economic indicators coming out next month, such as producer and consumer price data, as well as the U.S. Presidential election on November 5, were likely to underpin volatilities, the trader noted.
Implied volatility for CBOT December T-bond futures options stood at about 11.0 percent, up about 0.2 point from late Friday levels. March was also a touch higher at 10.1 percent.
Traders said speculative interest focussed on December contracts, which expire on November 15.

"It's just right in the perimeter of not having too much theta decay (time decay), just so you can hold the options for a couple of days, but...gamma is so high," said Jim Grauer, president of Omnitrage.
A high-gamma position gains more from a swing in underlying prices but is vulnerable to time decay.

He said gamma could be an important factor for this week's trading because the anticipated breakout could be a modest, short-lived one, like the move that followed the Federal Open Market Committee meeting in September.

Even though the futures markets rose 1-1/2 points immediately after the FOMC meeting, it was not enough to make a December 108-112 strangle, bought when futures were at 110, very profitable, Grauer recalled.
In Eurodollar futures options, implied volatility for March contracts rose slightly to about 14.5 percent.

A lot of the larger trades in Eurodollars today appeared to be expecting a continuation of range-trading, although there was also persistent demand for strangles and straddles, said a bank trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Among the largest deals, an investment bank was said to have bought 3,000 legs of January 94.25 straddles and sold 3,000 March straddles, a net long gamma play.
"I personally think the market is going to move quite a bit...but I also think some people are arguing it's still a range-trade and you actually have more downside potential," the bank trader said.
